questions.question: The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum which is invested for 5 years at a certain rate per cent p. a. is Rs. 9,800 and the amount payable on the same sum invested for 10 years at the same rate is Rs. 12,600. If simple interest is offered in both cases, the rate of interest p. a. is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple interest remains constant for every year.

SI for 5 years = A₁₀ − A₅ = 12600 − 9800 = ₹2800

Principal (P) = A₅ − SI for 5 years = 9800 − 2800 = ₹7000

SI for 1 year = 2800 ÷ 5 = ₹560

Rate % = (SI for 1 year ÷ P) × 100 = (560 ÷ 7000) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 5 years (A₅) = ₹9800

Amount after 10 years (A₁₀) = ₹12600

**Formula Used:**

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

questions.question: Raju is twice as skilled worker as Shaju. If both of them together can complete a work in 12 days, then in how many days will Raju alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Efficiency Ratio** of **Raju** : **Shaju** = 2 : 1

Combined Efficiency = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Days = 3 × 12 = 36 units

Raju alone = Total Work ÷ Raju's Efficiency = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency of **Raju** = 2 × Efficiency of **Shaju**

Time taken together = 12 days

 
 **Person** **Efficiency** **Total Work** **Days Taken** 
 **Raju** 2 36 36 ÷ 2 = 18 
 **Shaju** 1 36 ÷ 1 = 36 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Shaju's efficiency be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Raju's efficiency = 2 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of (Raju + Shaju) = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Total Work = Total Efficiency × Total Time

⇒ Total Work = 3 × 12 = 36 units.

⇒ Time taken by **Raju alone** = Total Work ÷ Raju's Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of efficiency is x : y, then the ratio of time taken is y : x.

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. This is the fundamental constant used to solve most **Time and Work** problems.

Combined Work

When multiple people work together, their individual efficiencies are added to find the net efficiency per day.</p

questions.question: Ram covers a certain distance D by car A at 15 kmph, an equal distance D by car B at 30 kmph and another equal distance D by car C at 5 kmph. If the total time of travel is 81 hours, then find the total distance cover by Ram. (in km)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ram covers a certain distance D by car A at 15 kmph,

An equal distance D by car B at 30 kmph

Another equal distance D by car C at 5 kmph.

The total time of travel is 81 hours.

**Concept used:**

Time = frac{ {Distance}}{ {Speed}}

**Calculation:**

The time required to cover distance D by car A = frac{ {D}}{15} hours

The time required to cover distance D by car B = frac{ {D}}{30} hours

The time required to cover distance D by car C = frac{ {D}}{5} hours

According to the question,

⇒ frac{ {D}}{15} +frac{ {D}}{30}+frac{ {D}}{5} = 81

⇒ frac{ {2D + D + 6D}}{30} = 81

⇒ frac{ {9D}}{30} = 81

⇒ D = 81 × (30)/(9) = 270 km

The total distance covered by Ram = 3 × 270 = 810 km

∴** The total distance covered by Ram is 810 km.**

questions.question: Mohan goes to office from home at a speed of 20 km/h and returns to home from office at a certain speed. If the average speed is 24 km/h, then what is the speed while returning?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Speed from home to office = 20 km/h

Average speed = 24 km/h

**Concept:**

Let the speed while returning from the office to home be denoted by x. We can use the concept of average speed to set up an equation and solve for x.

**Solution:**

The formula for average speed is given by:

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

where a and b are the speeds of two different segments.

Using the given data, we have:

24 km/h = (2 × 20 km/h × x)/(20 km/h + x)

Simplifying this equation, we find:

480 km/h + 24x km = 40x km/h

16x = 480

x = 30 km/h

**Therefore, the speed while returning is 30 km/h.**

questions.question: A retailer permits a trade discount of 25% followed by a cash discount of 8% on the already discounted price of his goods, and still makes a net gain of 17.3% of the cost price. At what percentage above the cost price of the goods is the marked price fixed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.

Successive discounts = 25% and 8% ⇒ Total **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 × 0.75 × 0.92 = 69.

Given **Gain** = 17.3%, so SP = 1.173 × **Cost Price (CP)**.

69 = 1.173 × CP ⇒ CP = 69 ÷ 1.173 = 58.823.

Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = [(100 − 58.823) ÷ 58.823] × 100 = 70%.

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Trade Discount = 25%, Cash Discount = 8%, Profit = 17.3%.

**Formulas:** Effective Discount = a + b − (a × b)/100 | MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/820e0e13acab7dd53dfb7a7e99173eec5f680e1f869a1c1c884c6274a4dcbfa6.png] 

⇒ Effective Discount = 25 + 8 − (25 × 8)/100 = 33 − 2 = 31%.

⇒ Let CP = 100, then SP = 100 + 17.3 = 117.3.

⇒ SP is after 31% discount on MP: 117.3 = MP × (100 − 31)/100.

⇒ 117.3 = MP × 0.69 ⇒ MP = 117.3 ÷ 0.69 = 170.

⇒ Markup percentage = MP − CP = 170 − 100 = 70%.

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between MP and CP

The ratio of **Marked Price** to **Cost Price** is directly given by (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.</p

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers 960 and 1020 is:
questions.solution:

questions.question: The weights of the five friends are 67 kg, 85 kg, 70 kg, 90 kg, and 103 kg. Find the average of their weights in kg.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a **base average** of 80 kg.

Calculate **deviations**: (67−80), (85−80), (70−80), (90−80), (103−80) → −13, +5, −10, +10, +23.

Sum of **deviations** = −13 + 5 − 10 + 10 + 23 = +15.

**Average deviation** = 15 ÷ 5 = +3.

**Actual Average weight** = Base + Average deviation = 80 + 3 = 83 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 83 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weights of five friends = 67 kg, 85 kg, 70 kg, 90 kg, and 103 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ebb2877ca123094278cf5be8d16a65ecc3f98bf2261f3ea7b716c65a13ff99f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Weight = 67 + 85 + 70 + 90 + 103

⇒ Total Weight = 415 kg

⇒ Total Number of friends = 5

⇒ Average weight = 415 ÷ 5

⇒ Average weight = 83 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 83 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Observations

The sum of observations is always equal to the **Average × Number of observations**.

Property of Deviation

The algebraic sum of the **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero.

Effect of Constant on Average

If every observation in a data set is **increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided** by a constant 'k', the average is also changed by the same constant 'k'.</p

questions.question: A person sold a refrigerator at a loss of 14%. Had he sold it for Rs. 805 more, he would have gained 6 %. What should be the selling price (in Rs.) to gain a profit of 11%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage difference = 6% (**Gain**) − (−14% **Loss**) = 20%.

According to the question, 20% of **Cost Price** (CP) = Rs. 805.

1% of CP = 805 ÷ 20 = Rs. 40.25.

To gain a **profit** of 11%, the required **selling price** must be 111% of CP.

Required SP = 40.25 × 111 = Rs. 4,467.75.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4,467.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Loss** = 14%, New **Gain** = 6%, Increase in **SP** = Rs. 805, Target **Profit** = 11%.

**Formula Used:** Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss %)/100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/197cf2957c51fc4e46c39388c7770637683f4a2a01be6340516993027c97f963.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price** be 100 units.

⇒ First Selling Price (SP₁) = 100 − 14 = 86 units.

⇒ Second Selling Price (SP₂) = 100 + 6 = 106 units.

⇒ Difference in Selling Prices = 106 − 86 = 20 units.

⇒ According to the question: 20 units = Rs. 805.

⇒ 1 unit = 805 ÷ 20 = Rs. 40.25.

⇒ Cost Price (100 units) = 40.25 × 100 = Rs. 4,025.

⇒ Target Selling Price (111 units) = 111 × 40.25 = Rs. 4,467.75.

Thus, the required price to gain 11% **profit** is Rs. 4,467.75, which corresponds to **Option 4**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4,467.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation for CP

When the difference between two selling prices (one at loss and one at gain) is given, CP = (Difference in SP ÷ Total % difference) × 100.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Change

If there are successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a × b)/100] %.</p

questions.question: If 1 + x² + x⁴ = 585 and 1 - x + x² = 65, then find the value of 1 + x + x².
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Algebraic Identity**: (1 + x + x²) × (1 − x + x²) = 1 + x² + x⁴

Substitute the given values into the formula: (1 + x + x²) × 65 = 585

Calculate the required value: 1 + x + x² = 585 ÷ 65

1 + x + x² = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

1 + x² + x⁴ = 585

1 − x + x² = 65

**Formula Used:**

The **fourth-power polynomial identity** is: a⁴ + a²b² + b⁴ = (a² + ab + b²)(a² − ab + b²)

For a = x and b = 1, the identity becomes: x⁴ + x² + 1 = (x² + x + 1)(x² − x + 1)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1 + x + x²) × (1 − x + x²) = 1 + x² + x⁴

⇒ (1 + x + x²) × 65 = 585

⇒ 1 + x + x² = 585 ÷ 65

⇒ 1 + x + x² = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Polynomial Identity

The expression x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴ can always be factored as (x² + xy + y²)(x² − xy + y²).

Sum and Difference Relations

If A = (x² + x + 1) and B = (x² − x + 1), then the **linear term** can be found as x = (A − B) ÷ 2.

Quadratic Component

The **quadratic sum** (x² + 1) can be found as (A + B) ÷ 2, where A and B are the factors of (x⁴ + x² + 1).</p

questions.question: The capacity of Q is 40% of that of P. P and Q can complete a piece of work in 12 days. In how much time can Q alone do it?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of efficiencies of **P** and **Q** = 100 : 40 = 5 : 2.

Combined efficiency = 5 + 2 = 7 units/day.

Total work = Combined efficiency × Total days = 7 × 12 = 84 units.

Time taken by **Q alone** = Total work ÷ Efficiency of Q = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Efficiency of Q is 40% of P.

⇒ Efficiency **Q/P** = 40/100 = 2/5

⇒ If efficiency of **P** = 5, then efficiency of **Q** = 2

⇒ Combined Efficiency (P + Q) = 5 + 2 = 7

⇒ Total Work = (Efficiency of P + Q) × Days = 7 × 12 = 84 units

⇒ Days required by **Q alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Days = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 days

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the work done or in the ratio of the efficiencies if time period is same.

Combined Work Formula

If A takes 'a' days and B takes 'b' days, together they take (a × b) ÷ (a + b) days.</p

questions.question: The least value of 2sin²theta + 3 cos²theta is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression: 2sin²theta + 3 cos²theta

**Formula used:**

We know that sin²theta + cos²theta = 1

**Calculations:**

Let x = sin²theta. Then, cos²theta = 1 - x.

Substituting in the given expression:

⇒ 2x + 3(1 - x) = 2x + 3 - 3x = 3 - x

The expression is 3 - x, where the maximum value of x is 1 and the minimum value is 0.

For the minimum value of the expression, x = 1:

⇒ 3 - 1 = 2

**∴ The least value is 2.**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP and MP Relationship

There is a direct relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price when profit and discount percentages are given: CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated by the formula: (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: A certain sum of money, when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, amounts to Rs 1,102 in 2 years and Rs 1,600 in 5 years. What is the principal amount (in Rs):
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money, when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, amounts to Rs 1,102 in 2 years and Rs 1,600 in 5 years.

Concept used:

Final Amount = Principal + Simple interest incurred for a particular period of time 

Calculation:

Interest incurred on the sum for 3 years = 1600 - 1102 = Rs. 498

Hence, Interest incurred on the sum for 2 years = (498 ÷ 3) × 2 = Rs. 332

Thus, The principal amount = 1102 - 332 = Rs. 770

**∴ The principal amount is Rs. 770.**

questions.question: Two stations A and B are 230 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 4 a.m. and travels towards B at 40 km/hr. Another train starts from B at 5 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 55 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by **Train 1** from 4 a.m. to 5 a.m. = 40 km/hr × 1 hr = 40 km.

Remaining distance at 5 a.m. = 230 − 40 = 190 km.

**Relative speed** (opposite directions) = 40 + 55 = 95 km/hr.

Time to meet from 5 a.m. = 190 ÷ 95 = 2 hours.

Meeting time = 5 a.m. + 2 hours = 7 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd83e302b983813ce045a7a126ec7541d07e369e5fb2f103f02b2b67537170b4.png] 

**Given:**

Total distance between **Station A** and **Station B** = 230 km.

Speed of **Train A** = 40 km/hr (starts at 4 a.m.).

Speed of **Train B** = 55 km/hr (starts at 5 a.m.).

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we make the start time of both trains the same (5 a.m.).

⇒ Distance covered by **Train A** in 1 hour (from 4 to 5 a.m.) = Speed × Time = 40 × 1 = 40 km.

⇒ Remaining Distance to be covered after 5 a.m. = 230 − 40 = 190 km.

⇒ Since trains are moving in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = SA + SB

⇒ Relative Speed = 40 + 55 = 95 km/hr.

⇒ Time taken to meet = Remaining Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 190 ÷ 95 = 2 hours.

⇒ Meeting Time = 5 a.m. + 2 hours = 7 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Same Direction Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the **difference** of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Time of Meeting

To calculate the **Meeting Time**, the distance between the objects must be considered from the point in time when both objects start moving simultaneously.</p

questions.question: The compound interest (compounding annually) on a certain sum for 2 years at the rate of 60 percent per annum is Rs. 6240. What will be the simple interest on the same sum for 3 years at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Compound interest (CI) = Rs. 6240

Time for CI (n1) = 2 years

Rate of interest (R) = 60% per annum

Time for simple interest (n2) = 3 years

**Formula**

CI/SI = 1 + R/200 (for only 2 years)

SI = PRT/100

**Solution:**

CI/SI = 1 + R/200

6240/SI = 1 + 60/200

SI = 4800

So SI for 2 years = 4800

SI = PRT/100

4800 = (P × 60 × 2)/100

P = 4000

SI for 3 years

SI = (4000 × 60 × 3)/100 = 7200.

**Therefore, the simple interest on the same sum for 3 years at the same rate of interest is Rs. 7200.**

questions.question: The angles of elevation of the top of an inaccessible tower from two points on the same straight line from the base of the tower are 30° and 60° respectively. If the points are separated at a distance of 100 m, then the height of the tower is close to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two points on the same side of a tower with distance **d** and angles **θ₁** and **θ₂**:

Height **h = d ÷ (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)**

h = 100 ÷ (cot 30° − cot 60°)

h = 100 ÷ (√3 − 1/√3) = 100 ÷ (2/√3) = 50√3

h = 50 × 1.732 = 86.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 86.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between points (**AB**) = 100 m

Angle at A (θ₁) = 30°, Angle at B (θ₂) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdadc27903f61df76d2173a5f3e95be086f19d9299bf85150700f7a1d174f6a5.png] 

Let the height of the tower be **h** and distance from the base to point **B** be **x**.

In triangle with 60°:

⇒ tan 60° = h ÷ x

⇒ √3 = h ÷ x ⇒ x = h ÷ √3

In triangle with 30°:

⇒ tan 30° = h ÷ (x + 100)

⇒ 1/√3 = h ÷ (h/√3 + 100)

⇒ h/√3 + 100 = h√3

⇒ 100 = h√3 − h/√3

⇒ 100 = h(3 − 1) ÷ √3

⇒ 100 = 2h ÷ √3

⇒ h = 50√3 = 50 × 1.732

⇒ h = 86.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 86.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Points on Opposite Sides

If points are on opposite sides of the tower, the distance **d = h(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂)**.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation from an observer's eye to the top of an object is always equal to the angle of depression from the top of the object to the observer's eye.

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values: **tan 30° = 1/√3**, **tan 45° = 1**, **tan 60° = √3**.</p

questions.question: What is the HCF of 144, 360 and 504?
questions.solution:
Given:

144, 360 and 504

Concept used:

HCF (Highest Common Factor) of two or more numbers is the greatest factor that divides the numbers.

Calculation:

144 = 2⁴ × 3²

360 = 2³ × 3² × 5

504 = 2³ × 3² × 7

Hence, HCF (144, 360, 504) = 2³ × 3² = 72

**∴ 72 is the HCF of 144, 360 and 504.**

questions.question: If k is product of smallest and greatest of the number (1)/(8), -(1)/(6), 25%, 0.33, -(3)/(8), then find the value of (12.5% of k × -64).
questions.solution:
Given:

The given numbers are: (1)/(8), -(1)/(6), 25%, 0.33, -(3)/(8)

Calculation:

The given numbers are: (1)/(8), -(1)/(6), 25%, 0.33, -(3)/(8)

The given numbers can be written as: (1)/(8), -(1)/(6), (1)/(4), (1)/(3), -(3)/(8)

Make the value of the denominator be the same for every fraction.

The L.C.M of (8, 6, 4, 3) = 24

Now, 

(3)/(24), -(4)/(24), (6)/(24), (8)/(24), -(9)/(24)

Now, arrange the above set of values in ascending orders.

-(9)/(24), -(4)/(24), (3)/(24), (6)/(24), (8)/(24)

It can be written as:

-(9)/(24) 

Or it can be written as:

-(3)/(8) 

Now, 

The value of the smallest number = -(3)/(8)

The value of the largest number = (1)/(3) = 0.33

The product of the smallest and largest number, k = -(3)/(8) × (1)/(3) = -(1)/(8)

Now, substitute the value of the respective variable in the required expression. 

⇒ (12.5% of -(1)/(8) × -64)

⇒ ((1)/(8) of -(1)/(8) × -64)

⇒ (1)/(64) × 64 = 1

∴ The required value of the expression is 1.

questions.question: The ages of two persons differ by 30 years. If 5 years ago, the elder one was 3 times as old as the younger one, then the present age of the younger person is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **age difference** remains constant at **30 years** regardless of the time period.

5 years ago, Ratio of **Elder : Younger** = 3 : 1.

Difference in ratio parts = 3 − 1 = 2 units → 30 years.

1 unit = 15 years. So, Younger person 5 years ago was 15 years old.

Present age of younger person = 15 + 5 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference in ages = 30 years; 5 years ago ratio = 3 : 1.

**Formula:** Age = (Ratio × Value) + Years passed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f7aae19c8a813050d1183a228d95e08d59922e71ba0eca4464276bfbc579579.png] 

⇒ Let the age of the **younger person** 5 years ago be x.

⇒ Age of the **elder person** 5 years ago = 3x.

⇒ Difference = 3x − x = 30

⇒ 2x = 30

⇒ x = 15 years (Age 5 years ago).

⇒ Present age of younger person = x + 5 = 15 + 5 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people **never changes** over time. If the difference is 30 now, it was 30 ten years ago and will be 30 ten years hence.

Ratio and Proportion in Ages

When a ratio is given for a past or future time, always translate the variables to that specific time period first to simplify the **linear equation**.</p

questions.question: A vessel contains liquid A and liquid B in the ratio 4 ∶ 9. If 8 litres of liquid A is added to the vessel, the new ratio becomes 8 ∶ 9. Find the quantity of liquid A (in litres) in the original mixture.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio **A : B** = 4 : 9

Final Ratio **A : B** = 8 : 9

Since only **Liquid A** is added, **Liquid B** remains constant (9 units).

Increase in A = 8 − 4 = 4 units → 8 litres.

1 unit = 2 litres ∴ Original A = 4 units = 4 × 2 = 8 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Ratio of **Liquid A** and **Liquid B** = 4 : 9

Amount of **Liquid A** added = 8 litres

New Ratio of **Liquid A** and **Liquid B** = 8 : 9

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da704161afa79dd3f9b061e66c6b9f38a0e9837c8b3790bea18b2d00534a6557.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Quantity of substance = Ratio part × Constant factor (x)

**Calculations:**

Let the initial quantities of **Liquid A** and **Liquid B** be 4x and 9x respectively.

⇒ (4x + 8) / 9x = 8 / 9

⇒ 9 × (4x + 8) = 8 × 9x

⇒ 36x + 72 = 72x

⇒ 72x − 36x = 72

⇒ 36x = 72

⇒ x = 2

⇒ Original quantity of **Liquid A** = 4x = 4 × 2 = 8 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 8 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Balancing Method

When one quantity in a ratio remains constant, multiply the ratios by suitable numbers to keep that quantity's units equal across both states.

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

Mixture problems often use percentages. Remember that x% = x/100, which can be simplified to a ratio for faster calculation.

Replacement Formula

Final Quantity = Initial Quantity × (1 − x/V)ⁿ, where x is the volume replaced and V is the total volume.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a book at 30% discount and still manages to earn 40% profit. In the next year, he give 10% discount on the book of same marked price and still manage to earn 50% profit. Find the per cent increase in the cost price of the book in the next year.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** is given by (100 − D%) : (100 + P%).

Year 1: CP₁ : MP = (100 − 30) : (100 + 40) = 70 : 140 = 1 : 2 = 5 : 10.

Year 2: CP₂ : MP = (100 − 10) : (100 + 50) = 90 : 150 = 3 : 5 = 6 : 10.

Since **MP** is same, **CP** increases from 5 to 6 units.

Percentage increase in CP = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First year: **Discount** = 30%, **Profit** = 40%

Next year: **Discount** = 10%, **Profit** = 50%, **Marked Price** is constant.

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5713e6cf42cd39430f7b9a9638b4cf5ecc74022305d8c2980add1cdfecccbf54.png] 

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** of the book be 100.

⇒ Year 1: SP₁ = 100 × (100 − 30) ÷ 100 = 70

⇒ Year 1: CP₁ = (70 × 100) ÷ (100 + 40) = 7000 ÷ 140 = 50

⇒ Year 2: SP₂ = 100 × (100 − 10) ÷ 100 = 90

⇒ Year 2: CP₂ = (90 × 100) ÷ (100 + 50) = 9000 ÷ 150 = 60

⇒ Increase in CP = CP₂ − CP₁ = 60 − 50 = 10

⇒ Percentage increase in CP = (10 ÷ 50) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is always CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This is the most efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit.

Marked Price (MP)

MP is the price set by the seller, usually higher than CP. Discounts are always calculated on the MP, while Profit or Loss is always calculated on the CP.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.</p

questions.question: A sum of money compound interest annually, the principal becomes Rs 30,250 in 2 years and Rs 33,275 in 3 years. Then find the principal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of Interest = [(Amount in 3 years − Amount in 2 years) ÷ Amount in 2 years] × 100

Rate = [(33,275 − 30,250) ÷ 30,250] × 100 = (3,025 ÷ 30,250) × 100 = 10%

Principal = Amount in 2 years ÷ (1 + r/100)²

Principal = 30,250 ÷ (1.1)² = 30,250 ÷ 1.21 = 25,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹30,250

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹33,275

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where **P** is **Principal**, **r** is **Rate**, and **n** is **Time**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/381b242cfd6ccbf02ee4569862879629f4117de6fd32a976eb395646ba67f40d.png] 

⇒ For consecutive years, **Rate** (r) = [(A₃ − A₂) ÷ A₂] × 100

⇒ r = [(33,275 − 30,250) ÷ 30,250] × 100

⇒ r = (3,025 ÷ 30,250) × 100 = 10% per annum

⇒ Now, using A₂ = P(1 + r/100)²

⇒ 30,250 = P(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ 30,250 = P(11/10)²

⇒ 30,250 = P × (121/100)

⇒ P = (30,250 × 100) ÷ 121

⇒ P = 250 × 100 = 25,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest on Consecutive Years

When interest is compounded annually, the **Amount** at the end of any year serves as the **Principal** for the next year. Thus, r = (Interest of 1 year ÷ Amount of previous year) × 100.

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate of r% compounded annually for 2 years, the effective rate on the principal is [2r + (r²/100)]%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** for 2 years is P(r/100)².

Face Diagonal of a Cube

Volume of a Cube

questions.question: M alone can complete a work in 50 days and N alone can complete the same work in 100 days. If both of them work together, then in 25 days what percent work of the total work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

M can complete a work in 50 days.

N can complete the same work in 100 days.

Both work together for 25 days.

**Concept:**

The work completed is the product of rate and time.

**Solution:**

⇒ Rate of M = 1/50 per day, rate of N = 1/100 per day.

⇒ Rate of M and N together = rate of M + rate of N = 1/50 + 1/100 = 3/100 per day.

⇒ Work completed in 25 days = Rate × time = 3/100 × 25 = 0.75 = 75%

**Therefore, 75% of the total work will be completed in 25 days.**

questions.question: X and Y can complete a certain work in 45 days and 60 days, respectively. They started the work together but X left after some days and Y alone completed the remaining work in 39 days. For how many days did X work?

Number of days X worked = 63 ÷ (4 + 3) = 9 days.
